cards.text: In those days, a preacher named John the Baptist shows up, preaching in the wilderness of Judea. No stage, no building, just John and a whole lot of nothing.

cards.question: John the Baptist's message is short: the kingdom of heaven is near. So what does he tell people to do?

cards.text: Matthew says John is the one the prophet Isaiah spoke of long ago, a voice calling in the wilderness. John showed up right on cue, friend, and I can't even show up on cue to my own oven timer.

cards.question: John says the kingdom of heaven is near. In Isaiah's words, the voice in the wilderness calls for a way to be prepared. Who is it prepared for?

cards.text: John wears a garment of camel's hair, with a leather belt around his waist. This man did NOT dress up for anybody.

cards.question: Out in the wilderness, what does John the Baptist eat?

cards.text: Locusts and wild honey. Friend, that's not a menu, that's a DARE. So who's making the trip out to this man?

cards.question: Only a few people go out to John the Baptist in the wilderness.
The people who come to John are baptized by him in the Jordan River while confessing their sins.

cards.text: Then John sees many of the Pharisees and Sadducees, two groups of Jewish religious leaders, coming to where he's baptizing. I bet the whole riverbank went quiet.

cards.question: When John sees the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his place of baptism, what does he call them?

cards.text: Not "good morning." Not "welcome." Straight to SNAKES. Then John asks them, "who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?"

cards.question: John tells the Pharisees and Sadducees to produce ___ in keeping with repentance.

cards.text: Then John shuts down an excuse before anybody can even say it out loud. That's a boss saying, "Don't even tell me it was traffic," before you walk in the door.

cards.question: Abraham is the ancestor of Israel's people. John warns the Pharisees and Sadducees not to count on having Abraham as their father.
John says that out of these ___, God can raise up children for Abraham.

cards.text: Then John paints a picture. The axe lies ready at the root of the trees.

cards.question: In John's picture of the axe at the root, what happens to every tree that doesn't produce good fruit?

answers.text: It is cut down and thrown into the fire
It is dug around and given another year
It is left standing alone in the field

cards.text: Now John the Baptist talks about Someone who will come after him. And this is where it gets good, friend.

cards.question: John says the One coming after him is less powerful than he is.
John says he isn't even worthy to do what for the One coming after him?

cards.text: John is the one baptizing everybody, and he says he's not worthy to carry this Man's SANDALS. Meanwhile, I stamp ONE straight cookie and I want a parade.

cards.question: John baptizes with water for repentance. What does he say the One coming after him will baptize with?

cards.text: Then John paints a harvest picture. The One coming has His winnowing fork in His hand, ready to clear His threshing floor.

cards.question: In John's harvest picture, the One coming will gather His ___ into the barn, but He will burn up the ___ with unquenchable fire.

cards.text: At that time, Jesus, who is called Christ, comes from Galilee to the Jordan, right where John is.

cards.question: Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan to be baptized by John.

cards.text: But John tries to stop Him. I think John is standing in that river wondering if this is really happening.

cards.question: When John tries to stop Jesus from being baptized, what does John say?

answers.text: I need to be baptized by You
You must go back to Galilee

cards.text: Jesus answers him, "Let it be so now," and then, "It is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness in this way."

cards.question: After Jesus answers, John still refuses to baptize Him.

cards.text: As soon as Jesus is baptized, He goes up out of the water. And SUDDENLY, the heavens are opened.

cards.question: Jesus sees the Spirit of God descending like a ___ and resting on Him.

cards.text: Like a dove, friend, and my Minty is shaped like a dove, so you KNOW I lean in close every time I read this. Then a voice from heaven speaks.

cards.question: After Jesus comes up out of the Jordan, what does the voice from heaven say?

answers.text: This is My beloved Son in whom I am well pleased
This is My chosen servant who will rule the nations
This is the prophet who will lead My people home

findings.problem: This story card repeats the answer from card 6 ('Locusts and wild honey') and adds a reaction, but tells no new part of the passage. Its only forward motion is a transition question.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences: 'Locusts and wild honey.' / 'Friend, that's not a menu, that's a DARE.' / 'So who's making the trip out to this man?'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Matthew 3:5 names where the crowds come from: Jerusalem, all Judea and the whole region around the Jordan. No card ever tells this. The true or false card only establishes that it isn't 'a few people', so the baker leaves without the scale and places the verse gives.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card has four sentences: 'Not "good morning."' / 'Not "welcome."' / 'Straight to SNAKES.' / 'Then John asks them...'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: No card sets up the fruit picture before this blank. Card 12 ends on 'the coming wrath', so the baker can only guess the wording 'fruit' over 'offerings' or 'promises'. The fruit image first appears in verse 10, later in the stop.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin calls the claim in verse 9 'an excuse'. The text calls it something they would 'presume to say to yourselves'. That is a presumption or claim, not an excuse.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: Nothing before this card points toward 'stones'. With 'waters' and 'hills' as options at a river in the wilderness, the baker is guessing unseen wording, not reasoning out meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The choice card introduces Abraham with a fact from outside the passage ('Abraham is the ancestor of Israel's people') and gives no reference for it. Choice cards cite only the verses of the right answer, so there is no place to put the reference.
findings.question: When a new person first appears on a choice card and needs an outside fact to introduce them, how should that fact be referenced? Should the introduction move to a story card instead?

findings.problem: This story card restates card 3's answer (not worthy to carry His sandals) and adds a joke, but tells no new part of verse 11.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: 'John is the one baptizing everybody' is stated as fact. It stretches verses 5 and 6, which name people from Jerusalem, Judea and the region around the Jordan.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Jesus is introduced as 'Jesus, who is called Christ', which comes from Matthew 1:16. The card cites only Matthew 3:13, so the outside fact has no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Story card 8 already says Jesus comes from Galilee to the Jordan, 'right where John is'. That gives away almost all of the true or false statement on card 9. Only 'to be baptized' is left, and it follows trivially from the setup.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The Minty line at the climax is warm but not funny. It reads like a nice dad being pleasant, and the card doesn't go for a real laugh.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
